title: Aether-Quanta and Fourier: Runtime Invariants and Algorithmic Bounds in Chronos-Interpreter
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We investigate a Chronos-Interpreter implementation that couples a balanced search structure with discrete Fourier analysis, termed Aether-Quanta Fourier. The design integrates a height-balanced tree for indexing transform coefficients while preserving the strict key-ordering invariant. We analyze asymptotic complexity, prove invariant preservation, and evaluate empirical performance on a single-core Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C system. The mean latency of 58.2 \textmu{}s per transform and a throughput of 17,178 ops/s confirm the practicality of the approach. This work demonstrates that a balanced indexing layer can coexist with Fourier computation without compromising theoretical guarantees or runtime efficiency. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261101_210224_xkcd_and_fourier}
